source: Brief NB2/briefs/TASK-110-a1.md; round-07 placement review; TASK-108 ledger rules.forTask110; TASK-109 ledger; running summary.

rules.matchersWeakenedNote: No matcher is loosened. The parser comparison (rules.selfCheck) lists every build and base read not present verbatim in the body that stays; each is (a) the same read on Round 7’s subject or helper (a renamed helper: routeShown for rounds(), routeTimer for timer(), the card’s “Log results” for timedLogOpener, `closeLog` for a click), (b) a Round 7 look or wording rewrite under the owner’s rule, listed in rules.forTask115, (c) an R7-3 retirement (rules.retiredAssertions), or (d) a base read over AmrapBlock/EmomBlock superseded by a port. Two regex reads introduced while porting were made exact again before hand-back (the For Time caption “Finished”, the one-round line). One read is stronger than the build’s (the EMOM rest window once, `toHaveLength(1)`). No `getBy` became `queryBy`, no `not` read was removed, no count dropped.
rules.testUpdateRule: Eric, chat, 2026-11-23: “Yes, approve” (standing test-update rule: update an old or base test to match Round 7’s look and wording, or drop only the look/wording part where Round 7 has no equivalent; keep everything else; list each change for UAT).

retiredAssertions.test: the window closing > ends on its own when the block’s seconds have passed, and only then offers the result
retiredAssertions.assertion: “08:00 on the clock”; “AMRAP complete”; no timer once ended
retiredAssertions.reason: R7-3 (Eric, chat, 2026-11-20: “Great, go ahead please”): Round 7’s accepted AMRAP clock replaced the readout; it stays and shows the window left (“Time complete”). For TASK-115’s UAT list.

retiredAssertions.test: the window closing > shows the elapsed time when the user finishes early, not the cap
retiredAssertions.reason: R7-3, as above. The elapsed time is still read, as what the block supplies to the shell.

retiredAssertions.test: surviving a refresh > comes back into the completion state when the buzzer went while it was away
retiredAssertions.reason: R7-3, as above; Round 7’s clock comes back reading “Time complete”.

forTask115: R7-3 (three AMRAP bodies): Round 7’s AMRAP clock stays after the window and after Finish early, showing the window left; the old “NN:NN on the clock” readout is retired. The carried base body “does not call an early finish a cap” still asserts that readout over AmrapBlock (round-07 N11).

The circuit card (Workout, and the circuit-round gallery state) now reads `CIRCUIT` in its badge and `3 ROUNDS` on a line under the header (was `CIRCUIT · 3 ROUNDS` outside the product presentation; under it Round 7 showed no rounds before one was recorded). TASK-107’s circuit-round parity receipts describe the older card (TASK-115 recaptures them, as TASK-108 noted).
A live EMOM with a rest window states “Ns rest at the end of each minute” on its prescription line after its window (“10 MIN · 15s rest at the end of each minute”).

Round 7’s format-only badge names any ladder rep scheme LADDER (glyph rule), so a circuit with a ladder-down scheme is badged LADDER although the circuit renderer performs it; `structureIdentity.format` still names LADDER only when the ladder renderer performs the block. The restored SectionHeader body reads LADDER for that circuit.

Wording read in ported/rewritten tests: “Minute N of M” (for MIN N OF M), “Minute 1 of 10 · Rest” (REST), “Time complete” (COMPLETE, AMRAP complete), “AMRAP time”/“EMOM time”/“FOR TIME time” (Time remaining), `01 hollow body hold` (1. hollow body hold), “Min 1 · 8 reps”, “Start FOR TIME”, `15 MIN CAP` (15:00 cap), `8 MIN` (As many rounds as possible in 08:00.), “4 rounds · 10:00 cap” (…on the whole ladder), `10 reps` (3 × 10 reps), “One round: 01 → 02 — no rest between movements”, “Finished” (Finished under cap), the note dialog “Movement note” with its field named by the movement (Notes — back squat).

Look read in ported/rewritten tests: live timed rows are named by a name line, not a heading; the blank AMRAP count is a quiet dash named “… : not recorded”; the AMRAP card has no “Each round:” heading; the prescription line sits under the header in the card, not inside the header; the header keeps a (never-used) flex-wrap in its column.

Behaviour noted, already Round 7’s: the timed end log opens itself when the clock ends during the visit (not on arrival after); before Start an EMOM marks its second movement Next (A3 TASK-117); the circuit-round dialog etc. unchanged.

selfCheck.method: Mechanical: every test file and e2e spec touched since 9c9db333 (9) parsed with the TypeScript compiler API; full titles (describe > … > it) at the base, the build (181e580) and this tree; for every body whose text differs from the base, the outermost expect(…) chains of the body and of the file helpers it calls (transitively) were printed canonically and compared, as sets, with the build’s and the base’s body of the same title. Each read not present verbatim was read and classified (see matchersWeakenedNote).
